The cost of running AI just dropped by an order of magnitude — and most enterprise AI budgets have not caught up to what that means.

Model routing is now saving 60% to 90% of inference costs by intelligently directing each query to the most cost-effective model capable of handling it. Simultaneously, OpenAI has cut its own inference costs by 2x through internal optimizations. DeepSeek's DSpark speculative decoding is pushing costs even lower, part of a broader pattern where Chinese AI labs are delivering competitive performance at a fraction of the price.

For CTOs managing AI infrastructure spend, this is a fundamental shift. The assumption that frontier AI capability requires frontier AI pricing is collapsing. Model routing means enterprises no longer need to send every request to the most powerful — and most expensive — model. The vast majority of production workloads can be handled by smaller, cheaper models with no loss in output quality.

The strategic implications are significant. First, AI projects that were previously uneconomical at scale become viable overnight. Second, organizations still running single-model architectures are overspending by a factor of 5 to 10 on inference. Third, the competitive pressure from Chinese labs offering equivalent capability at lower cost is accelerating the deflationary trend across the entire AI stack.

The executives who restructure their AI architecture around these cost realities now will free up budget to invest in AI applications that drive revenue — instead of burning capital on undifferentiated inference.
